title: Corporate Website Pixel-Perfect Build Business Definition

businessObjectives.objective: Deliver the corporate recruitment website so that stakeholders can use the supplied design as the production-facing experience without visual reinterpretation.
businessObjectives.businessValue: Preserves brand intent, reduces design-to-build rework, and enables the site to represent FABBI recruitment consistently.
successMeasures: All supplied public recruitment pages are implemented.
Manual visual approval is achieved for desktop 1440px and 1920px.
Stakeholders do not identify material deviations from the provided design.

businessObjectives.objective: Deliver the CMS/admin surface from the design so authorized users can access recruitment administration pages through login.
businessObjectives.businessValue: Establishes a controlled operational surface for managing recruitment-related content and submissions.
successMeasures: All supplied CMS/admin pages are implemented.
Login-to-admin journey is accepted in QA.

businessObjectives.objective: Ensure designed forms support real submission behavior backed by Supabase.
businessObjectives.businessValue: Turns the website from a static brochure into a usable recruitment channel.
successMeasures: Designed forms submit successfully to Supabase-backed behavior.
Failed submissions show an understandable outcome.
Submission behavior does not degrade visual parity.

businessObjectives.objective: Deliver the website using the existing Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind foundation.
businessObjectives.businessValue: Reduces delivery risk and avoids re-platforming work unrelated to business goals.
successMeasures: The implementation remains compatible with the project setup.
New technology choices are limited to requirement-driven needs.

kpis.name: Desktop visual approval
kpis.evidence: Manual QA record supported by screenshots

kpis.name: Form submission usability
kpis.target: 100% of designed forms have accepted submit behavior
kpis.evidence: QA confirms Supabase-backed submit success/failure behavior

kpis.name: CMS access control journey
kpis.evidence: QA confirms unauthenticated users do not directly enter CMS

stakeholders.name: Business owner
stakeholders.interest: Site represents company and recruitment brand correctly

stakeholders.name: Recruitment team
stakeholders.interest: Candidates can browse jobs and submit applications

stakeholders.name: CMS/admin users
stakeholders.interest: Can access and use admin pages after login

stakeholders.name: Engineering owner
stakeholders.interest: Site is maintainable and aligned to current stack

roles.name: Public visitor
restrictions: Cannot access CMS/admin pages without login

roles.name: Candidate
restrictions: Cannot access CMS/admin pages without authorized login

roles.name: CMS user
permissions: Access CMS/admin pages after Supabase Auth login
restrictions: Access is limited to authenticated admin surface

businessProcesses.name: Public recruitment browsing process
businessProcesses.description: A public visitor browses recruitment pages, reads company/job/news content, and follows design-provided navigation or CTAs.
businessProcesses.trigger: Visitor lands on a public recruitment page.
businessProcesses.outcome: Visitor can reach relevant public pages and understand available recruitment content.

businessProcesses.name: Candidate form submission process
businessProcesses.description: A candidate fills out a designed form and submits it through Supabase-backed behavior.
businessProcesses.trigger: Candidate submits a public recruitment form.
businessProcesses.outcome: Submission succeeds or fails with a visible user outcome.

businessProcesses.name: CMS access process
businessProcesses.description: A CMS user logs in with Supabase Auth before accessing CMS/admin pages.
businessProcesses.trigger: User attempts to access CMS/admin functionality.
businessProcesses.outcome: Authenticated CMS users can access admin pages; unauthenticated users cannot directly enter the CMS surface.

businessProcesses.name: Visual approval process
businessProcesses.description: Implemented pages are reviewed against the supplied design at desktop widths and approved manually.
businessProcesses.trigger: A page or surface is ready for QA.
businessProcesses.outcome: Page is either approved or returned for correction with visual deviations noted.

businessProcesses.name: Design-order delivery process
businessProcesses.description: Work proceeds according to the order of files in .design, unless dependency order requires a documented exception.
businessProcesses.trigger: Implementation planning or page delivery sequencing begins.
businessProcesses.outcome: Delivery remains aligned to the selected business priority order.

businessRules.rule: The supplied HTML/CSS design and screenshot references define the intended business appearance of the site.
businessRules.rationale: Pixel-perfect fidelity is the primary business requirement.

businessRules.rule: Screenshot comparison may support review, but final visual pass/fail is determined by manual approval.
businessRules.rationale: The blocker decision selected manual approval over strict numeric tolerance.

businessRules.rule: Public recruitment pages must be accessible without CMS/admin login.
businessRules.rationale: Public visitors and candidates need direct access to recruitment content.

businessRules.rule: Forms represented in the design must not remain static-only if they imply submission.
Form persistence and CMS authentication should use Supabase for this phase.
businessRules.rationale: The blocker decision selected Supabase and Supabase Auth.

businessRules.rule: A user submitting a form must receive a visible success or failure outcome.
businessRules.rationale: Submissions need business-operable feedback and cannot fail silently.

businessRules.rule: CMS/admin pages must be treated as protected operational surfaces rather than public pages.
businessRules.rationale: CMS surfaces are for authorized operational users.

businessRules.rule: CMS users must authenticate through Supabase Auth before CMS/admin access is granted.
businessRules.rationale: The blocker decision selected Supabase Auth for CMS login QA and access behavior.

businessRules.rule: Desktop visual acceptance must include both 1440px and 1920px viewport widths.
businessRules.rationale: These are the agreed desktop QA targets.

businessRules.rule: Subjective improvements, rebranding, or modernization cannot replace the supplied design without explicit approval.
businessRules.rationale: The business objective is to reproduce the provided design.

businessRules.rule: Implementation should follow the observed order of .design files unless an exception is documented.
businessRules.rationale: The blocker decision selected design-file order as the delivery sequence.

businessRules.rule: Re-platforming is not part of this business requirement.
businessRules.rationale: Keeping the current stack limits delivery risk and scope expansion.

useCases.name: Visitor views public recruitment homepage
useCases.goal: View the public recruitment homepage matching the supplied design.
useCases.mainSuccessOutcome: Visitor sees the design-faithful homepage and can use visible navigation/CTAs.
acceptanceCriteria: Visual appearance receives manual approval at required desktop widths.
Primary navigation and CTAs are available.

useCases.name: Visitor browses public content pages
useCases.goal: Navigate between recruitment, company, job, and news content represented in the design.
useCases.mainSuccessOutcome: Visitor reaches public content pages and sees content matching the design references.
acceptanceCriteria: Public pages represented in .design/recruitment_site are reachable.
Visible content and layout match design references.
Public browsing does not require CMS login.

useCases.name: Candidate submits a recruitment form
preconditions: Candidate is on a page with a designed form.
useCases.mainSuccessOutcome: Candidate submits the form and receives a visible success or failure outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: The form submits through Supabase-backed behavior.
The user sees the submission outcome.
The form remains visually faithful to the design.

useCases.name: CMS user logs in and views dashboard
preconditions: CMS user has valid Supabase Auth access for QA/use.
useCases.mainSuccessOutcome: CMS user authenticates and reaches the CMS dashboard/admin surface.
acceptanceCriteria: Authenticated CMS user can reach the dashboard/admin surface.
CMS pages match supplied design references.

useCases.name: Visual approver reviews a completed page
useCases.goal: Approve or reject visual fidelity for a completed page.
preconditions: Page is implemented and available in a running app.
useCases.mainSuccessOutcome: Page is manually approved or returned with deviations to fix.
acceptanceCriteria: Screenshot comparison or browser inspection evidence is available.
Final decision is manual approval or rejection.

useCases.name: CMS user reviews operational CMS pages
useCases.goal: Navigate through implemented CMS/admin pages after login.
useCases.mainSuccessOutcome: CMS user can reach CMS pages represented in the design.
acceptanceCriteria: CMS pages from .design/cms_site are reachable after login.
CMS navigation between admin pages is available.
CMS content structure matches the design source.

businessAcceptanceCriteria: All public recruitment design pages are implemented and reachable.
All CMS/admin design pages are implemented and reachable only after login.
Designed forms submit through Supabase-backed behavior and show visible outcomes.
Desktop visual QA at 1440px and 1920px receives manual approval.
The provided design is not reinterpreted, rebranded, or replaced by generic UI.
The existing Next.js/React/TypeScript/Tailwind stack remains the implementation foundation.

risks.risk: Pixel-perfect expectations are subjective without numeric tolerance
risks.mitigation: Use screenshot comparison as evidence and final manual approval as the business decision

risks.risk: Design HTML may not map cleanly to production app behavior
risks.mitigation: Treat design as source of truth while implementing safely and documenting deviations

risks.risk: Supabase setup may be unavailable or incomplete
risks.mitigation: Confirm Supabase project credentials before integration work begins

risks.risk: CMS auth expectations may expand beyond login gating
risks.mitigation: Keep this phase limited to Supabase Auth-gated access unless new requirements are approved

risks.risk: Full mobile parity may be assumed later
risks.mitigation: State desktop-first acceptance and handle mobile/tablet parity as a later requirement if needed

risks.risk: Design-order delivery may conflict with shared layout dependencies
risks.mitigation: Allow documented dependency-driven exceptions without changing business priority order
